report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of 2 of daedalus/structcore/cache.py. Contains get_many, put_many, prune, close, context manager methods. Claims in prune docstring verified as kept; other claims refer to outside code.
risks: get_many | low | Silently ignores corrupt rows (pass) – may hide data integrity issues. | Add logging or counter for corrupt rows.
put_many | low | Silently ignores exceptions; caller unaware of failures. | Consider raising or logging.
prune | low | Silently ignores exceptions; caller unaware of failures. | Consider raising or logging.
close | low | Silently ignores exception on close; may leak resources. | Consider logging.

handoff.purpose: Implements batch retrieval, batch insertion, pruning, and cleanup for the file analysis cache.

symbols.name: get_many
symbols.note: Retrieves multiple file analyses by keys; returns dict of key to FileAnalysis; silently skips corrupt rows.

symbols.name: put_many
symbols.note: Inserts or replaces multiple entries; silently ignores errors.

symbols.name: prune
symbols.note: Deletes rows whose keys are not in live_keys; uses temp table for efficiency.

symbols.name: close
symbols.note: Closes the database connection if open; sets conn to None.

symbols.name: __exit__
symbols.note: Context manager exit; calls close() and returns False.

claims.text: Drop rows for content no longer present, so the DB tracks the repo's current state instead of growing without bound across edits.
claims.why: The code deletes rows from files whose key is not in live_keys, exactly as claimed.

claims.text: Chunked to stay under SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER on big repos.
claims.why: The code uses chunks of 500, which is a common limit, but the actual SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: corrupt row -> treat as a miss, recompute
claims.why: The except block passes silently, effectively treating corrupt rows as missing.

observations.what: get_many uses string formatting for SQL query; safe because keys are not user input but still not best practice.
put_many uses executemany with INSERT OR REPLACE; overwrites existing rows without warning.
prune creates a temp table 'live' but never drops it; may persist across calls.
All methods silently catch broad Exception; may hide programming errors.
